turns.speaker: Reisender
turns.german: Und wann fährt der nächste Zug nach Berlin?
turns.english: And when does the next train to Berlin leave?

turns.speaker: Auskunft
turns.english: It leaves at two p.m. (fourteen hundred).

blocks.title: Wie spät ist es?
blocks.bodyEnglish: 'Wie spät ist es?' is the standard way to ask the time. You'll also hear 'Wie viel Uhr ist es?' — both are correct, and nobody will blink at either.

blocks.headline: Die Zeitwörter
blocks.bodyEnglish: The words that carry every time question.

blocks.headline: halb neun ist 8:30
blocks.bodyGerman:
Es ist acht Uhr.            → 8:00
Es ist acht Uhr fünfzehn.   → 8:15
Es ist halb neun.           → 8:30
blocks.bodyEnglish: German tells time by counting TO the next hour. 'Halb neun' literally means 'half to nine' — so it's 8:30, not 9:30. This is the single most confusing clock pattern for English speakers.

blocks.headline: Der 24-Stunden-Tag
blocks.bodyEnglish: Germany runs on the 24-hour clock. TV guides, timetables, doctor's appointments and shop hours all use it — 'von 9 bis 18 Uhr'. In conversation people still say 'acht Uhr' for 8 a.m. and 'zwanzig Uhr' for 8 p.m.

blocks.explanationEnglish: Telling the time always uses 'sein' in third person singular: 'Es ist'. Add the hour, then the minutes. 'Halb N' means half an hour BEFORE N — it counts forward to the next hour, not back from the current one.
blocks.englishBridge: English: 'It's half past eight.' → German looks ahead: 'Es ist HALB NEUN' (half [to] nine). Same moment, opposite direction.

blocks.title: halb neun ≠ 9:30
blocks.bodyEnglish: 'halb neun' is 8:30, not 9:30 — it counts forward to the next hour. And it is always 'Es ist', never 'Es hat'.

blocks.prompt: Ordne die Wörter zu einem richtigen Satz.
blocks.explanationEnglish: 'um' comes before the clock time, and the 24-hour clock is standard on timetables.

items.hint: the standard way to ask the time

blocks.explanationEnglish: 'Halb neun' counts forward to the next hour: half [to] nine = 8:30.

blocks.prompt: A train leaves at 14:00. Choose the right sentence:
options: Der Zug fährt um vier Uhr.
Der Zug fährt um vierzehn Uhr.
Der Zug fährt vierzehn Uhr um.
blocks.explanationEnglish: Timetables use the 24-hour clock, and the preposition 'um' comes before the time: 'um vierzehn Uhr'.

blocks.promptEnglish: Build: 'Der Zug fährt um vierzehn Uhr.'

blocks.title: Uhrzeit in einer Zeile
bullets: halb neun = 8:30 (zählt zum nächsten Vollständigen vor).
Am Fahrplan gilt der 24-Stunden-Tag: um vierzehn Uhr.
